steps.step_text: Collect Arabidopsis xylem exudate for nano-liquid chromatography-tandem mass spectrometry (nano-LC–MS/MS) analysis.
steps.step_rationale: To explore whether the Arabidopsis CLE peptide is translocated from roots to shoots via the xylem, Arabidopsis xylem exudate was collected for nano-LC–MS/MS analysis.
steps.span_chunk: To explore whether the Arabidopsis CLE peptide is translocated from roots to shoots via the xylem, we collected Arabidopsis xylem exudate and performed nano-liquid chromatography-tandem mass spectrometry (nano-LC–MS/MS) analysis

steps.step_text: Perform nano-LC–MS/MS analysis on the collected xylem exudate to detect the presence of mature CLE2 peptide.
steps.step_rationale: The nano-LC–MS/MS analysis is used to detect the peak that corresponds to the mature CLE2 peptide from Arabidopsis xylem exudate, which supports the root-to-shoot translocation of Arabidopsis CLE peptides.
steps.span_chunk: We indeed detected a peak of m/z 863.4 at 9.0 min that corresponded to this mature CLE2 peptide from Arabidopsis xylem exudate. The MS/MS spectrum of this peak showed a fragmentation pattern coinciding with that of the 12-amino acid arabinosylated CLE2 peptide.

steps.step_text: Analyze the MS/MS spectrum of the detected peak to confirm the identity of the mature CLE2 peptide.
steps.step_rationale: The MS/MS spectrum analysis is necessary to confirm that the fragmentation pattern of the detected peak coincides with that of the 12-amino acid arabinosylated CLE2 peptide, thus validating the presence of the CLE2 peptide in the xylem exudate.
steps.span_chunk: The MS/MS spectrum of this peak showed a fragmentation pattern coinciding with that of the 12-amino acid arabinosylated CLE2 peptide.

steps.step_text: Prepare a cell suspension from planaria.
steps.step_rationale: A cell suspension is required to perform the staining procedure.
steps.span_chunk: The cell suspension of planaria was stained with Hoechst 33,342 (nuclear dye) and MTG.

steps.step_text: Stain the cell suspension with Hoechst 33342 to label the nuclei.
steps.step_rationale: Hoechst 33342 is a nuclear dye that allows for the identification of different cell populations based on their nuclear content.
steps.span_chunk: The cell suspension of planaria was stained with Hoechst 33,342 (nuclear dye) and MTG.

steps.step_text: Stain the cell suspension with MTG to measure the mitochondrial mass.
steps.step_rationale: MTG is a fluorescent dye used to measure mitochondrial mass, which is an indicator of the stem versus differentiated state of the cells.
steps.span_chunk: This was tested by staining the neoblast population with MTG, a fluorescent dye that is used as a measure for the mitochondrial mass.

steps.step_text: Prepare a cell suspension of planaria and stain the cells with Hoechst 33,342 (nuclear dye) and MTG (mitochondrial dye).
steps.step_rationale: To visualize and differentiate the planarian cell populations based on their nuclear content and mitochondrial mass for flow cytometry analysis.
steps.span_chunk: The cell suspension of planaria was stained with Hoechst 33,342 (nuclear dye) and MTG.

steps.step_text: Run the stained cell suspension through a flow cytometer to identify the three distinct populations X1, X2, and Xins based on their nuclear content and mitochondrial mass.
steps.step_rationale: Flow cytometry allows for the identification and quantification of different cell populations by measuring the fluorescence intensity of the dyes that bind to specific cell components.
steps.span_chunk: The cells stained with Hoechst showed three distinct populations, X1, X2, and Xins, based on their nuclear content.

steps.step_text: Analyze the flow cytometry data to determine the MTG signal distribution and fluorescence intensity in the X1, X2, and Xins populations.
steps.step_rationale: The MTG signal distribution and fluorescence intensity provide information on the mitochondrial mass of the cells, which is indicative of their stem versus differentiated state.
steps.span_chunk: X1 cells, which are the proliferating stem cells, have a lower MTG signal than the Xins population (differentiated cells). The X2 population, majorly neoblast progenitor, had a broad distribution of the MTG signal.

steps.step_text: Confirm the mitochondrial mass findings by treating the cells with Verapamil, an efflux pump inhibitor, and re-staining with MTG if necessary.
steps.step_rationale: To test whether the low MTG intensity in X1 and X2 cells was a consequence of dye efflux and to confirm that the lower MTG fluorescence is a true indicator of decreased mitochondrial mass.
steps.span_chunk: To test whether the low MTG intensity in X1 and X2 cells was a consequence of dye efflux, the cells were treated with Verapamil, an efflux pump inhibitor, and stained with MTG.

steps.step_text: Prepare a cell suspension of planaria and stain it with Hoechst 33342 and MitoTracker Green (MTG).
steps.step_rationale: To visualize and differentiate the cell populations based on nuclear content and mitochondrial mass.
steps.span_chunk: The cell suspension of planaria was stained with Hoechst 33,342 (nuclear dye) and MTG.

steps.step_text: Analyze the stained cells using flow cytometry or fluorescence microscopy to identify the three distinct populations: X1, X2, and Xins, based on their nuclear content.
steps.step_rationale: To categorize the cells into different populations for further analysis of mitochondrial mass.
steps.span_chunk: The cells stained with Hoechst showed three distinct populations, X1, X2, and Xins, based on their nuclear content (Figure 1 A).

steps.step_text: Examine the MTG fluorescence in X1 cells and note the perinuclear and polarized distribution of the signal in the cytoplasm.
steps.step_rationale: To assess the mitochondrial distribution pattern in proliferating stem cells (X1 cells).
steps.span_chunk: MTG fluorescence in most X1 cells was more perinuclear and exhibited polarized distribution in the cytoplasm (Figures 1 D and S1).

steps.step_text: Examine the MTG fluorescence in Xins cells and observe the even distribution of the signal throughout the cytoplasm.
steps.step_rationale: To determine the mitochondrial distribution pattern in differentiated cells (Xins cells).
steps.span_chunk: Conversely, MTG fluorescence in Xins cells, in general, was evenly distributed in the cytoplasm (Figures 1 D and S1).

steps.step_text: Document the fluorescence distribution patterns observed in X1 and Xins cells for comparison and analysis.
steps.step_rationale: To record the mitochondrial distribution patterns for further interpretation and to conclude the stem versus differentiated state based on mitochondrial mass.
steps.span_chunk: Together, these results suggest that the difference in the mitochondrial mass between X1 and Xins cells could be an indicator of the stem versus differentiated state.

steps.step_text: Prepare a cell suspension of planaria and stain with Hoechst 33,342 and MTG to identify distinct populations X1, X2, and Xins based on their nuclear content and mitochondrial mass.
steps.step_rationale: To visualize and differentiate the planarian cell populations based on nuclear content and mitochondrial mass for further analysis.
steps.span_chunk: The cell suspension of planaria was stained with Hoechst 33,342 (nuclear dye) and MTG.

steps.step_text: Treat the cells with Verapamil, an efflux pump inhibitor, to inhibit the dye efflux in X1 and X2 cells.
steps.step_rationale: To determine if the low MTG intensity in X1 and X2 cells is due to dye efflux by blocking the efflux pumps with Verapamil.
steps.span_chunk: To test whether the low MTG intensity in X1 and X2 cells was a consequence of dye efflux, the cells were treated with Verapamil, an efflux pump inhibitor, and stained with MTG.

steps.step_text: After treatment with Verapamil, stain the cells with MTG and analyze the median fluorescence intensity in the X1 population to assess changes in mitochondrial mass.
steps.step_rationale: To evaluate the effect of Verapamil treatment on mitochondrial mass by measuring the median fluorescence intensity of MTG in X1 cells.
steps.span_chunk: There was no significant increase in the median fluorescence intensity in the X1 population on treatment with Verapamil (Figure 1 E), suggesting that the lower MTG fluorescence in X1 cells is a true indicator of decreased mitochondrial mass.

steps.step_text: Isolate healthy intact myofibers from extensor digitorum longus (EDL) muscles.

steps.span_chunk: To exclude this possibility, we evaluated satellite cell activation using isolated healthy intact and damaged individual myofibers ( Figures 2 A and S1 A).

steps.step_text: Mechanically damage the isolated myofibers using a Pasteur pipette in a culture dish to obtain damaged myofibers.
steps.step_rationale: Damaged myofibers are needed to produce DMDFs that will be used to stimulate the satellite cells associated with the healthy intact myofibers.

steps.step_text: Co-culture the intact myofibers with the damaged myofibers to allow for the interaction of satellite cells with DMDFs.
steps.step_rationale: Co-culturing intact myofibers with damaged myofibers enables the examination of whether DMDFs directly stimulate the activation and proliferation of satellite cells associated with the healthy intact myofibers.
steps.span_chunk: This co-culture of intact myofibers with damaged myofibers allowed us to examine whether DMDFs directly stimulate the activation and proliferation of satellite cells associated with the healthy intact myofibers.

steps.step_text: Perform immunofluorescence analysis to detect the presence of MYOD+ satellite cells on intact myofibers after co-culturing with damaged myofibers for 48 and 72 hours.
steps.step_rationale: Immunofluorescence analysis is used to determine the effect of DMDFs on satellite cell activation by detecting the presence of MYOD+ satellite cells, which are markers for satellite cell activation.
steps.span_chunk: Immunofluorescence analysis revealed the presence of a higher proportion of MYOD+ satellite cells on intact myofibers when they were co-cultured with damaged myofibers at both 48 ( Figures 2 B and 2C) and 72 hours ( Figures 2 D and 2E) of culture compared with control conditions.

steps.step_text: Assess the proportion of Ki67+ satellite cells and cells positive for EdU to evaluate cell cycle entry and proliferation.
steps.step_rationale: The proportion of Ki67+ satellite cells indicates entry into the cell cycle, while EdU incorporation reflects S-phase entry, which is necessary to understand the proliferation status of satellite cells under the influence of DMDFs.
steps.span_chunk: Interestingly, the proportion of Ki67+ satellite cells was increased ( Figures 2 F and 2G), but that of cells positive for EdU, an S-phase cell-cycle entry marker, was unchanged under the co-culture conditions ( Figures 2 H and 2I).

steps.step_text: Co-culture intact myofibers with mechanically damaged myofibers isolated from extensor digitorum longus (EDL) muscles.
steps.step_rationale: This step is to examine whether damaged myofiber-derived factors (DMDFs) directly stimulate the activation and proliferation of satellite cells associated with the healthy intact myofibers.
steps.span_chunk: To exclude this possibility, we evaluated satellite cell activation using isolated healthy intact and damaged individual myofibers (Figures 2 A and S1 A). This co-culture of intact myofibers with damaged myofibers allowed us to examine whether DMDFs directly stimulate the activation and proliferation of satellite cells associated with the healthy intact myofibers.

steps.step_text: Incubate the co-culture for 48 to 72 hours.
steps.step_rationale: The incubation period is necessary to allow for the potential activation and proliferation of satellite cells due to the influence of DMDFs.
steps.span_chunk: Immunofluorescence analysis revealed the presence of a higher proportion of MYOD+ satellite cells on intact myofibers when they were co-cultured with damaged myofibers at both 48 (Figures 2 B and 2C) and 72 h (Figures 2 D and 2E) of culture compared with control conditions.

steps.step_text: Perform immunofluorescence staining on the co-cultured myofibers to detect MYOD+ and Ki67+ satellite cells.
steps.step_rationale: Immunofluorescence staining is used to visualize the presence and proportion of satellite cells that are activated (MYOD+) and those that have entered the cell cycle (Ki67+).
steps.span_chunk: Immunofluorescence analysis revealed the presence of a higher proportion of MYOD+ satellite cells on intact myofibers when they were co-cultured with damaged myofibers... Interestingly, the proportion of Ki67+ satellite cells was increased (Figures 2 F and 2G)...

steps.step_text: Analyze the immunofluorescence results to determine the effect of DMDFs on satellite cell activation and proliferation.
steps.step_rationale: Analyzing the results will provide insights into whether DMDFs induce satellite cells to enter the cell cycle and whether they stimulate activation and proliferation.
steps.span_chunk: These results, therefore, imply that DMDFs induce satellite cells to enter the cell cycle; however, the cells stay in the G1 phase of the cell cycle and do not undergo the S phase.

steps.step_text: Wash out the damaged myofibers and the culture media containing DMDFs from the co-culture.
steps.step_rationale: To remove the influence of DMDFs and damaged myofibers on the satellite cells and to prepare for the observation of reversibility of satellite cell activation.
steps.span_chunk: The damaged myofibers and the culture media containing DMDFs were then washed out and replaced with fresh DMEM and cultured for an additional 24 h (Figure 3 A).

steps.step_text: Replace the washed out media with fresh Dulbecco's modified Eagle medium (DMEM).
steps.step_rationale: To provide a clean environment with fresh nutrients and to observe if the satellite cells revert to a quiescent state without the influence of DMDFs.
steps.span_chunk: The damaged myofibers and the culture media containing DMDFs were then washed out and replaced with fresh DMEM and cultured for an additional 24 h (Figure 3 A).
steps.task_name: Wash out damaged myofibers and culture media

steps.step_text: Culture the intact myofibers in the fresh DMEM for an additional 24 hours.
steps.step_rationale: To allow time for the satellite cells to potentially revert to a quiescent state after the removal of DMDFs and damaged myofibers.

steps.step_text: Measure the transverse diameter of satellite cells associated with intact myofibers after co-culture with damaged myofibers and after washing out the damaged myofibers and culture media.
steps.step_rationale: Measuring the transverse diameter of satellite cells allows for the analysis of cell size changes, which is an indicator of satellite cell activation and reversibility to a quiescent-like state.

steps.step_text: Generate transgenic Drosophila melanogaster flies carrying a FLAG-tagged isoform of TBPH cloned in UAS expression vectors.
steps.step_rationale: To express the FLAG-tagged TBPH in neurons, transgenic flies with the appropriate construct are required.
steps.span_chunk: For these experiments, we expressed a FLAG-tagged isoform of TBPH in Drosophila neurons and performed pull-down assays from fly head tissues.

steps.step_text: Cross the transgenic flies carrying the FLAG-tagged TBPH construct with flies carrying the pan-neuronal driver elav-GAL4 or the motoneuronal promoter D42-GAL4.
steps.step_rationale: To drive the expression of the FLAG-tagged TBPH specifically in neurons, it is necessary to use neuronal promoters such as elav-GAL4 or D42-GAL4.
steps.span_chunk: Consequently, we found that the neuronal expression of two independent RNAi lines against gypsy utilizing the pan-neuronal driver elav-GAL4 or the more restricted motoneuronal promoter D42-GAL4 were able to significantly revert the locomotive phenotypes observed in TBPH-minus third instar larvae.

steps.step_text: Isolate the neurons from the heads of the resulting progeny to prepare for pull-down assays.
steps.step_rationale: Neuronal tissues are required for the pull-down assays to confirm the expression and function of the FLAG-tagged TBPH.
steps.span_chunk: For these experiments, we expressed a FLAG-tagged isoform of TBPH in Drosophila neurons and performed pull-down assays from fly head tissues.
